Overview: The Camano 28/31 Troll is a compact British Columbia-designed flybridge cruiser built around Bob Warman’s distinctive Keelform semi-displacement hull. The hull measures 28 feet on deck and roughly 31 feet overall, which explains the model’s changing 28, 30 and 31 marketing designations. A single diesel sits low in the keel and drives a protected shaft, while lower and upper helms, a bright deckhouse and one-cabin interior make the boat primarily a couple-oriented inland and coastal cruiser.

CoupleCruising.Summary: The documented layout is explicitly couple-oriented, with occasional guest berths rather than multiple private cabins.

SoloHandling.Summary: Compact dimensions, strong visibility and single-shaft propulsion support owner operation; docking conditions and thruster fit still matter.

InlandWaterways.Summary: The 10 ft 6 in beam, modest draft and efficient low-speed operation suit many inland routes; actual air draft must be verified.

ExposedWater.Summary: The Keelform hull, protected running gear and pilothouse support coastal use, but B-Atlas does not treat these models as unrestricted offshore passagemakers; condition, loading and weather limits remain decisive.

TradeOffs: Small cockpit and modest storage compared with wider cruisers
Steep flybridge ladder and upper-station exposure affect accessibility
One private cabin limits guest privacy
Production changes in engines and tankage require hull-number-specific verification
BestFor: Couples seeking an economical flybridge pocket trawler
Great Loop, inland-waterway and protected coastal cruising
Owner-operators valuing visibility, simple single-diesel propulsion and manageable dimensions

ModelVariations.Description: Early boats used smaller Volvo diesels, followed by 150 hp and then 200 hp Volvo six-cylinder installations; Volvo D4 and later Yanmar 6BY installations appear at the end of the production lineage.

The same family hull was marketed as the Camano 28 and later renamed Camano 31.
More than 270 Camano 31-family boats were built before the design lineage passed to Helmsman.
The Helmsman 31 Sedan is the modernized descendant of this hull.

Overview: The Carver 3607 Aft Cabin is a production aft-cabin motor yacht built around high interior volume, two-stateroom privacy and twin-engine coastal performance. Its multi-level deck plan trades easy all-on-one-level movement for substantial accommodation in a relatively modest overall length.

SoloHandling.Summary: Twin engines can assist close-quarters maneuvering, but size, windage and multi-level access increase workload.

InlandWaterways.Summary: Comfortable for inland cruising, but beam, air draft and fuel consumption must be checked against route and marina constraints.

ExposedWater.Summary: These are coastal production cruisers; actual capability depends on generation, loading, machinery, weather and individual condition.

ModelCharacter: A major 1980s Carver success built on a 'dual mode' modified-V hull that can cruise efficiently near hull speed yet still plane with enough power. Wide side decks, two-stateroom layouts and a lower helm make it unusually practical for an aft-cabin yacht.
DesignLineage: Introduced in 1982 as Carver's largest model at the time.
The same basic hull was later used for the Carver 36 Mariner.

Overview: The Nordic Tug 26 is the original compact Nordic Tugs cruiser, built around a pilothouse, semi-displacement fiberglass hull and single diesel shaft drive. Its narrow beam and one-cabin layout favor economical couple cruising, inland waterways and compact marina footprints rather than large-boat accommodation. Production was interrupted after 1997 and later revived in limited production, so displacement, engines and equipment vary materially by generation.

ModelCharacter: A rare late-1980s Chien Hwa-built Taiwan trawler marketed under the Sealord/Sea Lord name, using a traditional double-cabin layout, teak interior and low-powered twin diesels for approximately 6-knot cruising. It belongs to the broad CHB/Chien Hwa import tradition but is retained as a separate market identity because direct evidence does not prove it is merely a renamed CHB 34.
DesignLineage: Verified 1986 and 1987 Ontario examples establish a 34-foot Sealord/Sea Lord double-cabin or tri-cabin trawler identity.
A current 1987 listing explicitly identifies the builder lineage as 'Sealord (Chien Hwa) Trawler'.
Chien Hwa was one of Taiwan's major trawler builders and produced boats sold under numerous importer and distributor names.

Because no reliable source directly equates the Sealord 34 with B-Atlas's canonical CHB 34 Double Cabin, B-Atlas preserves it as a distinct record at Moderate confidence rather than merging on similarity alone.
OwnershipCharacter: Low-speed twin diesels, full displacement and a teak-rich interior make it an economical classic cruiser underway, but the age and low documentation level shift risk toward teak decks, deck core, tanks, windows and electrical systems. Builder-specific parts are effectively custom or owner-sourced.

ModelVariations.Name: 1984 36 II
ModelVariations.Description: A 36 II version appeared in 1984 with a fully cored hull, revised flybridge and interior, materially different from earlier solid-hull examples.

ModelCharacter: A durable Pacific Northwest aft-cabin motor yacht built around Uniflite's solid-fiberglass modified-V 36-foot hull. Its full-width aft master, lower helm, wide side decks and twin inboards made it an early high-volume family cruiser rather than a trawler, with gasoline performance commonly near 18 knots.
DesignLineage: The Uniflite 36 Double Cabin was produced from 1972 through 1984 on the same basic solid-fiberglass hull as the 36 Sport Sedan.
In 1984 Uniflite introduced a 36 II with a fully cored hull, revised flybridge and updated interior; this was a late-generation evolution within the 36 Double Cabin line.
When Uniflite closed in 1984, Chris-Craft acquired the molds and continued the design as the Catalina 36/362/370 family.
A cockpit derivative, the Uniflite 41 Yacht Fisherman, was created by extending the same aft-cabin concept with a working cockpit.
OwnershipCharacter: Straightforward twin-shaft machinery and solid early hull construction are positives, but these boats are now old enough that fuel tanks, wiring, windows, decks and prior repowers dominate condition. Uniflite's well-known blister problems require hull and topside inspection, especially on later fire-retardant-resin boats.

Overview: The Windy 26 SN is a Norwegian-built 26-foot hardtop pocket trawler/snekke from the early-to-mid 1980s. Its double-ended fiberglass hull combines a full-length skeg, aft bilge keels and single diesel shaft drive with a protected helm, large cockpit and compact overnight accommodation. Period testing emphasized unusually good stability, economical operation and easy low-speed handling for a boat of this size.

ModelCharacter: A rare Norwegian-built pocket trawler whose double-ended snekke-inspired hull, full-length skeg and single Volvo diesel deliver remarkable stability and economy in only 25½ feet. Its hardtop helm, large cockpit and U-shaped forward dinette make it a genuine tiny cruising boat rather than a fishing cuddy.
DesignLineage: Documented examples span 1981–1986.
A 1984 Canadian Yachting road test specifically describes the 26 SN as a diesel-powered small trawler.
The hull incorporates a full-length skeg plus small aft bilge keels for stability and tracking.
The SN belongs to Windy's older Scandinavian cruising lineage and bears little relationship to the brand's later high-performance sports cruisers.
OwnershipCharacter: Single shaft diesel, manual backup steering and tiny system count make it extremely economical. Scandinavian-specific fittings and age are the challenges; cabin size and standing headroom are naturally limited.
